name: search-engines-tab-to-youtube
description: Search engines plan: a seeded, enabled starter offers Tab-to-search on a fresh profile. Tasks 1-3 landed the model, C++ mirror, and settings pane; this is the first VM proof that a starter's keyword actually reaches TemplateURLService and the omnibox keyword provider offers it. The fixture carries no settings file, so the profile starts at searchEnginesSeed 0 and the C++ mirror seeds every starter, YouTube included, as enabled. Google stays the DEFAULT engine via seed_prefs, and a default engine is never offered for Tab-to-search, so this types the full keyword 'youtube.com' - KeywordProvider::GetTemplateUrlForText looks the text up as a keyword, it does not complete a prefix.

actions.note: GATE: the restored tab has committed, so the app is up and the profile is live
the reserved chrome context lands about 670ms after startup and the palette's WebContents needs it
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
let the /commandbar document commit and take the field
the keyword pass has to finish before any row can carry an engine
the row offering the scope, on an unscoped bar
the typed keyword resolved to a TemplateURL and the row carries it
THE CHIP, beside an emptied field - or the scope-less bar the bug leaves behind
the chip carries the engine's DISPLAY name, which only TemplateURLService knows
the scoped pass lands - the query it answers is 'youtube.com cats', not 'cats'

No www. The line is redacted through LogSafeUrl, which returns scheme plus the REGISTRABLE domain: GetDomainAndRegistry('https://www.youtube.com') is 'youtube.com', so the subdomain is gone from the log. The migration audit checked that no pattern expected a path after the host, and that a .localhost subdomain survives (it does, because GetDomainAndRegistry returns empty there and the bare host is used). A www. on a real registrable domain is the case neither check covered.

assertions.desc: a fresh profile seeds YouTube as enabled and the keyword provider offers it
Tab entered the scope and the chip names the engine, not the raw keyword
